### Variable Types

```{r, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse) 
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
```

```{r}
bigdata <- read.csv("tanaka_photoperiod_experiment_summer_2024 .csv", 
                    strip.white = TRUE, 
                    check.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}
names(bigdata)

researchdata <- data.frame(
  id.number = bigdata$id.number,
  beetle.number = bigdata$beetle.number,
  replicate = bigdata$replicate,
  day.of.experiment = bigdata$day.of.experiment,
  photoperiod = bigdata$photoperiod,
  light.status = bigdata$light.status,
  dispersal = bigdata$dispersal,
  burial = bigdata$burial,
  perched.on.stick.in.water = bigdata$perched.on.stick.in.water,
  perched.on.stick.out.of.water = bigdata$perched.on.stick.out.of.water
)

researchdata$photoperiod <- as.factor(researchdata$photoperiod)

researchdata$light.status <- as.factor(researchdata$light.status)
researchdata$light.status <- fct_recode(researchdata$light.status, 
                                   "On" = "1", 
                                   "Off" = "0")

researchdata$dispersal <- as.factor(researchdata$dispersal)
researchdata$dispersal <- fct_recode(researchdata$dispersal, 
                                   "Yes" = "1", 
                                   "No" = "0")

researchdata$burial <- as.factor(researchdata$burial)
researchdata$burial <- fct_recode(researchdata$burial, 
                                   "Yes" = "1", 
                                   "No" = "0")

researchdata$perched.on.stick.in.water <- as.factor(researchdata$perched.on.stick.in.water)
researchdata$perched.on.stick.in.water <- fct_recode(researchdata$perched.on.stick.in.water, 
                                   "Yes" = "1", 
                                   "No" = "0")

researchdata$perched.on.stick.out.of.water <- as.factor(researchdata$perched.on.stick.out.of.water)
researchdata$perched.on.stick.out.of.water <- fct_recode(researchdata$perched.on.stick.out.of.water, 
                                   "Yes" = "1", 
                                   "No" = "0")

```
```{r}
str(researchdata)
```

###  Clean up Numeric Variables

```{r}
summary(researchdata)
```

### Visualize Variables-Dispersal per Photoperiod Treatment 
```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Dispersal Mosaic - Filtered for rows 1102 to 1201
# Filter data for specified rows and remove NA values
filtered_data <- researchdata[1101:1201, ] %>%
  filter(!is.na(photoperiod) & !is.na(dispersal))

# CHI-SQUARE TEST AND ASSUMPTIONS CHECKING

# 1. Check data structure and create contingency table
contingency_table <- table(filtered_data$photoperiod, filtered_data$dispersal)
print("Contingency Table:")
print(contingency_table)

# 2. Check sample size assumption (n >= 30)
total_n <- sum(contingency_table)
cat("\nTotal sample size:", total_n)
if(total_n >= 30) {
  cat(" ✓ Sample size assumption met (n >= 30)\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Sample size assumption NOT met (n < 30)\n")
}

# 3. Check independence assumption
cat("\nIndependence Assumption:")
cat("\n- Observations should be independent")
cat("\n- Each subject should contribute to only one cell")
cat("\n- Random sampling should be used")
cat("\n✓ Assumed met based on experimental design\n")

# 4. Check expected frequency assumption (all expected frequencies >= 5)
expected_freq <- chisq.test(contingency_table)$expected
print("\nExpected Frequencies:")
print(round(expected_freq, 2))

min_expected <- min(expected_freq)
cat("\nMinimum expected frequency:", round(min_expected, 2))
if(min_expected >= 5) {
  cat(" ✓ Expected frequency assumption met (all cells >= 5)\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Expected frequency assumption NOT met (some cells < 5)\n")
  cat("Consider using Fisher's Exact Test instead\n")
}

# 5. Check for cells with expected frequency < 1
cells_less_than_1 <- sum(expected_freq < 1)
cat("Cells with expected frequency < 1:", cells_less_than_1)
if(cells_less_than_1 == 0) {
  cat(" ✓ No cells with expected frequency < 1\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Some cells have expected frequency < 1\n")
}

# 6. Perform Chi-square test
chi_test <- chisq.test(contingency_table)
print("\nChi-square Test Results:")
print(chi_test)

# 7. Calculate effect size (Cramér's V)
cramers_v <- sqrt(chi_test$statistic / (total_n * (min(dim(contingency_table)) - 1)))
cat("\nCramér's V (effect size):", round(cramers_v, 3))
if(cramers_v < 0.1) {
  cat(" (negligible effect)")
} else if(cramers_v < 0.3) {
  cat(" (small effect)")
} else if(cramers_v < 0.5) {
  cat(" (medium effect)")
} else {
  cat(" (large effect)")
}

# 8. Alternative tests if assumptions are violated
if(min_expected < 5 || cells_less_than_1 > 0) {
  cat("\n\nAlternative Test (Fisher's Exact Test):")
  if(nrow(contingency_table) == 2 && ncol(contingency_table) == 2) {
    fisher_test <- fisher.test(contingency_table)
    print(fisher_test)
  } else {
    cat("\nFisher's Exact Test not available for tables larger than 2x2")
    cat("\nConsider Monte Carlo simulation or combining categories")
  }
}

# 9. Summary of results
cat("\nChi-square statistic:", round(chi_test$statistic, 3))
cat("\np-value:", round(chi_test$p.value, 4))
if(chi_test$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat("\n✓ Significant association between photoperiod and dispersal (p < 0.05)")
} else {
  cat("\n✗ No significant association between photoperiod and dispersal (p >= 0.05)")
}
cat("\nEffect size (Cramér's V):", round(cramers_v, 3))

# Create summary data for plotting
mosaic_data <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(photoperiod, dispersal) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(photoperiod) %>%
  mutate(prop = count / sum(count),
         total = sum(count))

ggplot(mosaic_data, aes(x = factor(photoperiod), y = prop, fill = factor(dispersal))) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Dispersal Proportions by Photoperiod (Rows 1102-1201)",
    x = "Photoperiod (Hours of Light per Day)",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Dispersal"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "orchid", "Yes" = "#4ECDC4")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format())
```
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Create survival object using researchdata
researchdata$dispersal_numeric <- ifelse(researchdata$dispersal == "Yes", 1, 0)

# Adjust the Event column:
# - 1 = dispersed
# - 0 = censored (death or no event)
researchdata$AdjustedEvent <- ifelse(researchdata$dispersal == "Yes", 1, 0)

# Set 12-hour photoperiod as the reference level
researchdata$photoperiod <- relevel(researchdata$photoperiod, ref = "12")

# Check the structure again
table(researchdata$AdjustedEvent, researchdata$photoperiod)

# Create the survival object
surv_obj <- Surv(time = researchdata$day.of.experiment, event = researchdata$AdjustedEvent)

#Check for assumptions !!!!!
res.cox1 <- coxph(surv_obj ~ photoperiod, data = researchdata)
res.cox1
res.zph1 <- cox.zph(res.cox1)

# Fit Cox Proportional Hazards Model
cox_model <- coxph(surv_obj ~ photoperiod, data = researchdata)

# View summary of the model
cox_model

# Create survival object
surv_obj <- Surv(time = researchdata$day.of.experiment, 
                 event = researchdata$dispersal_numeric)

# Fit survival curves by photoperiod
surv_fit <- survfit(surv_obj ~ photoperiod, data = researchdata)

# Create the plot
ggsurvplot(
  surv_fit,
  data = researchdata,
  conf.int = TRUE,            # Add confidence intervals
  xlab = "Days",              # X-axis label
  ylab = "Proportion Not Dispersed",  # Y-axis label
  palette = "jco",            # Use a predefined color palette
  font.x = 14,                # Increase X-axis font size
  font.y = 14,                # Increase Y-axis font size
  font.tickslab = 12,         # Increase tick label font size
  legend.title = "Photoperiod (Hours)",  # Add legend title
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 8)  # Apply theme directly
)
```
```{r}
#Check for assumptions !!!!!
res.cox1 <- coxph(surv_obj ~ photoperiod, data = researchdata)
res.cox1
res.zph1 <- cox.zph(res.cox1)
res.zph1
```



### Visualize Variables-Burial per Photoperiod Treatment- day 3 
```{r, warning=FALSE}

# Filter data to only include Day 3
day3_data <- researchdata %>%
  filter(day.of.experiment == 3)

# Create summary data for mosaic plot
mosaic_data <- day3_data %>%
  group_by(photoperiod, burial) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(photoperiod) %>%
  mutate(prop = count / sum(count),
         total = sum(count))

# Plot
ggplot(mosaic_data, aes(x = factor(photoperiod), y = prop, fill = factor(burial))) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Burial Proportions by Photoperiod on Day 3",
    x = "Photoperiod (Hours of Light per Day)",
    y = "Proportion",
    fill = "Burial"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "orchid", "Yes" = "#4ECDC4")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format())

# CHI-SQUARE TEST AND ASSUMPTIONS CHECKING FOR BURIAL ON DAY 3

# 1. Check data structure and create contingency table
contingency_table <- table(day3_data$photoperiod, day3_data$burial)
print("Contingency Table:")
print(contingency_table)

# 2. Check sample size assumption (n >= 30)
total_n <- sum(contingency_table)
cat("\nTotal sample size:", total_n)
if(total_n >= 30) {
  cat(" ✓ Sample size assumption met (n >= 30)\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Sample size assumption NOT met (n < 30)\n")
}

# 3. Check independence assumption
cat("\nIndependence Assumption:")
cat("\n- Observations should be independent")
cat("\n- Each subject should contribute to only one cell")
cat("\n- Random sampling should be used")
cat("\n✓ Assumed met based on experimental design\n")

# 4. Check expected frequency assumption (all expected frequencies >= 5)
expected_freq <- chisq.test(contingency_table)$expected
print("\nExpected Frequencies:")
print(round(expected_freq, 2))

min_expected <- min(expected_freq)
cat("\nMinimum expected frequency:", round(min_expected, 2))
if(min_expected >= 5) {
  cat(" ✓ Expected frequency assumption met (all cells >= 5)\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Expected frequency assumption NOT met (some cells < 5)\n")
  cat("Consider using Fisher's Exact Test instead\n")
}

# 5. Check for cells with expected frequency < 1
cells_less_than_1 <- sum(expected_freq < 1)
cat("Cells with expected frequency < 1:", cells_less_than_1)
if(cells_less_than_1 == 0) {
  cat(" ✓ No cells with expected frequency < 1\n")
} else {
  cat(" ✗ Some cells have expected frequency < 1\n")
}

# 6. Perform Chi-square test
chi_test <- chisq.test(contingency_table)
print("\nChi-square Test Results:")
print(chi_test)

# 7. Calculate effect size (Cramér's V)
cramers_v <- sqrt(chi_test$statistic / (total_n * (min(dim(contingency_table)) - 1)))
cat("\nCramér's V (effect size):", round(cramers_v, 3))
if(cramers_v < 0.1) {
  cat(" (negligible effect)")
} else if(cramers_v < 0.3) {
  cat(" (small effect)")
} else if(cramers_v < 0.5) {
  cat(" (medium effect)")
} else {
  cat(" (large effect)")
}

# 8. Alternative tests if assumptions are violated
if(min_expected < 5 || cells_less_than_1 > 0) {
  cat("\n\nAlternative Test (Fisher's Exact Test):")
  if(nrow(contingency_table) == 2 && ncol(contingency_table) == 2) {
    fisher_test <- fisher.test(contingency_table)
    print(fisher_test)
  } else {
    cat("\nFisher's Exact Test not available for tables larger than 2x2")
    cat("\nConsider Monte Carlo simulation or combining categories")
  }
}

# 9. Summary of results
cat("\nChi-square statistic:", round(chi_test$statistic, 3))
cat("\np-value:", round(chi_test$p.value, 4))
if(chi_test$p.value < 0.05) {
  cat("\n✓ Significant association between photoperiod and burial (p < 0.05)")
} else {
  cat("\n✗ No significant association between photoperiod and burial (p >= 0.05)")
}
cat("\nEffect size (Cramér's V):", round(cramers_v, 3))

```

```{r}
environmentdata <- read.csv("Noelle_Tanaka_Photoperiod_evnironmental_var Summer 2024 - Photoperiod environmental variables.csv", 
                    strip.white = TRUE, 
                    check.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}
environmentdata$Photoperiod <- as.factor(environmentdata$Photoperiod)

# Create the plot without Time.of.day
ggplot(environmentdata, aes(x = Day, 
                            y = temperature, 
                            group = Photoperiod, 
                            color = factor(Photoperiod))) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Temperature Across Days by Photoperiod",
       x = "Day",
       y = "Temperature (°C)",
       color = "Photoperiod") +
  theme_minimal()

environmentdata$Photoperiod <- as.factor(environmentdata$Photoperiod)
environmentdata$Day <- as.factor(environmentdata$Day)  # or leave numeric if continuous

# One-way ANOVA for Temperature by Photoperiod
# Make sure your data is loaded first

# Run one-way ANOVA
anova_result <- aov(temperature ~ Photoperiod, data = environmentdata)

# Display ANOVA table with p-values
summary(anova_result)

# Alternative: You can also use oneway.test() for a one-way ANOVA
oneway.test(temperature ~ Photoperiod, data = environmentdata)

# For more detailed output, you can also use:
anova(anova_result)

# To check assumptions:
# 1. Check normality of residuals
shapiro.test(residuals(anova_result))

# 2. Check homogeneity of variances
bartlett.test(temperature ~ Photoperiod, data = environmentdata)

# Repeated Measures ANOVA using base R
# Replace "Subject" with the column identifying each participant or replicate

anova_rm <- aov(temperature ~ Photoperiod, data = environmentdata)

# View results
summary(anova_rm)

```
